rooms.title: Spotting the red flags
rooms.scene: For weeks, {p} has ditched movie nights, hibernated until noon, and completely ignored {their} guitar.
rooms.ask: What is your tactical opening move?

opts.t: Catch {them} in a quiet moment and say neutrally: “I've noticed your routine shifted a lot lately. How are you holding up beneath the surface?”
opts.why: Spotting lifestyle shifts without weaponizing them opens a low-pressure gateway for honesty.
opts.re: …You noticed? Honestly, not great. I didn't think anyone could tell.

opts.t: Challenge {them} to a low-stakes board game night to gently pull {them} back into a shared routine.
opts.why: Even micro-social obligations can feel like an impossible performance requirement when someone's battery is drained.
opts.re: A game night? Maybe… I just don't have much in me for fun right now.

opts.t: Mention casually: “You haven't touched that guitar in weeks.”
opts.why: Bare observations of skipped habits subtly point out their decline, creating quiet pressure and self-consciousness.
opts.re: …Yeah. I know. You don't have to point it out.

rooms.title: Reading the subtext
rooms.scene: You spot {p} slouching on the sofa under a blanket with noise-canceling headphones on, offering a microscopic, strained smile before looking at the floor.
rooms.cue: 🎧 Cocooned in a blanket burrito, eyes locked downward.
rooms.line: “Oh, hey. Just chilling, totally living my best lazy Sunday life.”
rooms.ask: Read the subtext. What's the optimal play here?

opts.t: Sit down a safe distance away and murmur: “Mind if I occupy space near you in absolute silence? Zero conversation required on your end.”
opts.why: Their brain capacity is maxed out. Quiet presence respects boundaries while proving they aren't stranded.
opts.re: …Yeah. Quiet sounds perfect. Thanks for not making me talk.

opts.t: Smile warmly: “No pressure to talk, but I'm going to put your favorite comfort show on softly.”
opts.why: Introducing external sensory stimuli forces an exhausted nervous system to process data when it needs static reduction.
opts.re: That's sweet… I'll probably zone out, but it's nice having it on.

opts.t: Look at the headphones and say: “Quiet day.”
opts.why: Using clipped minimalism to comment on withdrawal isolates them further by highlighting detachment without warmth.
opts.re: …Yeah. Quiet day.

rooms.title: The 'I'm Just Tired' Mask
rooms.scene: {P} has replied 'just tired' every single evening for three weeks while visibly losing weight and skipping tasks.
rooms.line: “Seriously, I just didn't sleep great last night. Stop looking at me like that.”
rooms.ask: How do you respond without triggering defensiveness?

opts.t: Soften your posture: “Fair enough, I'll back off. Just know if it ever turns out to be heavier than bad sleep, you don't have to carry it solo.”
opts.why: Respecting stated boundaries while leaving an unpressured door open preserves trust without forcing a confession.
opts.re: …Okay. Thanks for not pushing. Maybe it is more than sleep.

opts.t: “I'm only looking because I care—let me order you some melatonin and blackout curtains to fix your sleep.”
opts.why: Jumping straight into logistical problem-solving bypasses the emotional reality behind exhaustion.
opts.re: Thanks… but I don't think curtains will fix this.

opts.t: “You said the exact same thing yesterday.”
opts.why: Directly tracking and repeating past statements turns dialogue into a scoreboard, shutting down future disclosure.
opts.re: …I know. I'm sorry I keep saying it.

rooms.title: Cancelled Plans Pattern
rooms.scene: Ten minutes before a small dinner with close friends, {p} texts from the bed asking you to go alone and make up an excuse.
rooms.line: “Tell them I have a migraine. I just can't put a face on tonight.”
rooms.ask: What is your immediate move before leaving?

opts.t: Knock softly, peek in without lecturing: “I'll cover for you, no problem. Want me to bring back soup later, or leave it outside your door?”
opts.why: Removing social guilt and offering zero-demand care protects their dignity during an energy crash.
opts.re: …Thank you. Soup outside the door sounds perfect. Sorry, and thank you.

opts.t: Sit on the edge of the mattress: “I won't force you, just promise me you'll step outside for ten minutes while I'm gone.”
opts.why: Attaching wellness homework to a cancelled plan turns rest into another obligation they might fail.
opts.re: Ten minutes outside… I'll try. I can't promise.

opts.t: Reply: “I'll tell them you stayed home.”
opts.why: Neutral compliance delivers social news without support or warmth, leaving them to sit alone in isolation.
opts.re: …Okay. Have a good night.

rooms.title: The Sudden Silence
rooms.scene: Standing by the counter preparing lunch, {p} goes completely mute mid-sentence and stares blankly out the window.
rooms.cue: 👀 Shoulders slumped, jaw clenched, fingers stiff on the edge of the counter.
rooms.ask: How do you handle the sudden shift?

opts.t: Lower your voice slightly and say gently: “No rush to talk—we can just stand in quiet until you're ready.”
opts.why: Lowering sensory demand and removing conversational pressure lets their nervous system regulate safely.
opts.re: …Thanks. I just need a minute. You staying helps.

opts.t: Reach over and pat {their} arm: “Hey, where did your brain just go? Tell me what just popped into your head.”
opts.why: Demanding immediate verbalization when someone dissociates or hits a wave of numbness overwhelms them.
opts.re: I don't know where it went… I can't explain it right now.

opts.t: Keep wiping the counter and look straight ahead.
opts.why: Withholding visual engagement and maintaining absolute silence matches withdrawal with quiet indifference.
opts.re: …Never mind.

rooms.title: Brain Fog & Indecision
rooms.scene: You ask {p} what {they} want{s} to watch, and {they} freeze{s} for forty seconds, visibly distressed over choosing between two options.
rooms.line: “I don't know. Why is picking a show making me want to cry right now?”
rooms.ask: How do you relieve decision paralysis?

opts.t: Take the wheel calmly: “Decision fatigue is real. I'm putting on this movie—all you have to do is sit down.”
opts.why: Executive dysfunction makes trivial choices feel crushing; removing micro-decisions restores calm immediately.
opts.re: …Thank you. I just need someone else to choose right now.

opts.t: Smile encouragingly: “Take a deep breath! Let's flip a coin so you can practice quick low-stakes choices.”
opts.why: Turning cognitive overload into a 'skill-building exercise' misses that their brain is genuinely depleted.
opts.re: A coin… I can't even think straight, honestly.

opts.t: Stand quietly waiting for an answer.
opts.why: Patient silent waiting while someone experiences severe executive dysfunction increases internal pressure and inadequacy.
opts.re: …I'm sorry. I don't know. I just don't know.

rooms.title: Mounting Clutter
rooms.scene: Papers and notes have sat stacked in an unorganized pile on the desk for weeks, and {p} is staring at it looking defeated.
rooms.line: “I can't even sort a stack of notes. What is actually wrong with me?”
rooms.ask: What is the most supportive intervention?

opts.t: Sit on the chair beside the desk: “Depression turns small tasks into mountains. Want to just toss the junk in the bin together?”
opts.why: Lowering the standard and normalizing executive dysfunction removes shame.
opts.re: …Together? Okay. That actually feels doable.

opts.t: “You're just overwhelmed—set a fifteen-minute timer and sort just the top folder for a quick dopamine win!”
opts.why: Productivity hacks assume normal energy reserves and often leave depressed individuals feeling worse if they stall.
opts.re: Fifteen minutes… I'll try, but I'll probably stall again.

opts.t: Move around the desk to reach the bookshelf.
opts.why: Physical avoidance of the clutter while bypassing the person reinforces feelings of being an invisible obstacle.
opts.re: …Right. I'm in the way. Sorry.

rooms.title: Short, Flat Replies
rooms.scene: All week, {p}'s notes in your shared journal have shrunk to one-word answers, a sharp drop from expressive entries.

opts.t: Leave a low-friction note: “Hey, noticing your entries have been brief lately. Zero need to write a paragraph—just thinking of you.”
opts.why: Explicitly removing the obligation to reply prevents check-ins from becoming another unread chore.
opts.re: …Thank you. I read it three times. It helped more than you know.

opts.t: Write back: “You've seemed really distant this week—did something happen between us or are you having a rough patch?”
opts.why: Asking whether you caused the distance forces them to expend scarce energy reassuring you.
opts.re: It's not you… I just don't have words lately. I'm sorry.

opts.t: Leave a single checkmark symbol on the page.
opts.why: Responding to minimal communication with a non-verbal mark ends the loop, signaling acceptance of distance without care.
opts.re: …Okay. I guess that's that.

rooms.title: Hygiene Slippage
rooms.scene: You notice {p} has worn the same sweatpants for four days straight and hasn't brushed {their} hair.
rooms.ask: How do you offer gentle care without embarrassing {them}?

opts.t: Run a warm shower, lay out a clean towel and fresh hoodie without commentary, and say: “Bathroom's open if you want a reset—no pressure.”
opts.why: Setting up the environment quietly eliminates activation steps without drawing attention to appearance.
opts.re: …Thank you. A warm shower might actually help. No pressure helps more.

opts.t: Hand {them} a fresh outfit with a bright smile: “Come on, a hot shower will make you feel brand new!”
opts.why: Promising that basic hygiene will transform mood sets up unrealistic expectations and subtle judgment.
opts.re: Brand new… I wish. I'll try, I guess.

opts.t: Leave a towel on the mattress edge.
opts.why: Placing a bathroom item down without context creates unspoken behavioral prompting.
opts.re: …Okay. I get the hint.

rooms.title: Returning from Work
rooms.scene: {P} comes home from work, drops {their} bag, and sits down staring at the floor without moving.
rooms.line: “I spent eight hours pretending to be a functional human. I have nothing left.”

opts.t: Pour a glass of water and slide it over quietly: “You don't have to perform here. Take all the quiet time you need.”
opts.why: Acknowledging exhaustion and offering immediate physical comfort signals total safety.
opts.re: …Thank you. I don't have to pretend here. That means everything.

opts.t: “You did great getting through the day! Let's talk through what drained you most today.”
opts.why: Immediately asking them to recount stressors demands mental labor right when their tank hits zero.
opts.re: Can we talk later? I have nothing left for words right now.

opts.t: Walk past to check the mail on the counter.
opts.why: Stepping past someone sitting in heavy depletion to check mail communicates that routine tasks outrank their state.
opts.re: …Right. The mail.

rooms.title: Stealthy acts of service
rooms.scene: {P} hasn't eaten in twelve hours and is staring down a piece of plain toast like it requires advanced calculus.

opts.t: Quietly whip up something basic, place it nearby without commentary, and sit quietly without pressuring {them} to perform.
opts.why: Depression makes basic tasks feel mountainous. Quiet, low-friction help removes barriers without pressure.
opts.re: …Thanks. I can maybe manage a little of this, if no one's watching.

opts.t: Cut the toast into neat pieces and prompt: “Eat just three bites for me, okay? You'll feel better once blood sugar rises.”
opts.why: Setting micro-goals shifts focus to performance and creates a failure condition if they still can't eat.
opts.re: Three bites… okay. I'll try. It just feels like a lot.

opts.t: Walk away without speaking.
opts.why: Exiting the room while someone struggles silently with basic intake leaves them entirely unassisted.
opts.re: …Oh. You're going. Okay.

rooms.title: Countering the Burden Trap
rooms.scene: While scrubbing plates together by the sink, {p} stops dead, staring blankly at the soapy water.
rooms.line: “I'm so sorry. I am genuinely just a massive anchor dragging your entire life down.”
rooms.ask: How do you counter this emotional trap?

opts.t: Look {them} straight in the eye: “You aren't an anchor. We're riding out a brutal storm, and I'm right here in this boat with you voluntarily.”
opts.why: Feeling like a burden is a hallmark symptom of depression. Direct, unconditional reassurance cuts through distortion.
opts.re: …A storm. Okay. I really needed to hear you're still in the boat.

opts.t: Hold {their} wet hands gently: “I won't pretend this season hasn't stretched me thin—but I love you enough to push through.”
opts.why: Admitting how taxing they are right when they feel worthless confirms their darkest fear.
opts.re: …So I am stretching you thin. I knew it.

opts.t: Continue washing plates without looking up.
opts.why: Maintaining rhythmic chores through a vulnerable self-deprecation statement signals emotional detachment.
opts.re: …Yeah. I'll be quiet now.

rooms.title: Administrative Overwhelm
rooms.scene: A stack of unopened mail and an overdue bill reminder sit untouched on the desk.
rooms.line: “If I open those envelopes, I'm going to panic. I'm failing at basic adulthood.”
rooms.ask: How do you support {them} without taking over {their} autonomy?

opts.t: Pull up a chair beside {them}: “Want to sit together while I open the mail and sort junk, and we only look at one real letter?”
opts.why: Body-doubling and breaking down tasks preserves agency while sharing cognitive load.
opts.re: …One letter? Okay. I can do one with you here.

opts.t: Scoop up the stack: “Give those to me—I'll pay everything and handle your inbox from now on.”
opts.why: Over-functioning and stripping away all responsibility reinforces helplessness and breeds resentment.
opts.re: …Thanks. I guess I really can't even do this anymore.

opts.t: Place the mail upright in the organizer.
opts.why: Organizing paperwork silently without consultation bypasses agency and reinforces inadequacy.
opts.re: …Okay. Out of sight, out of mind, I guess.

rooms.title: Insomniac Spiral
rooms.scene: At 2:30 AM, {p} is wide awake scrolling on {their} phone after lying in the dark for hours.
rooms.line: “My brain refuses to shut off and tomorrow is already ruined.”

opts.t: Keep your voice low and calm: “Resting your body still counts. Want me to play a boring sleep podcast softly?”
opts.why: Removing pressure to force sleep reduces performance anxiety that keeps insomnia alive.
opts.re: …A boring podcast. Okay. Resting counts. I like that.

opts.t: “Put your phone away right now—blue light ruins melatonin and we need to fix your sleep hygiene.”
opts.why: Lecturing on sleep hygiene at 2:30 AM feels corrective rather than soothing.
opts.re: I know, I know… I just can't stop my head right now.

opts.t: Turn over and pull the blanket away from the light.
opts.why: Physical shielding against screen glow communicates sleep-disruption annoyance without words.
opts.re: …Sorry. I'll turn the light off.

rooms.title: Declining Help Out of Guilt
rooms.scene: You offer to pick up {p}'s prescription, and {they} immediately tense up on the couch.
rooms.line: “No, stop doing things for me. You're already doing everything and I feel pathetic.”
rooms.ask: How do you reframe accepting help?

opts.t: Keep it light and equal: “I'm driving past the pharmacy anyway—let me grab it so we both get an easier evening.”
opts.why: Framing help as ordinary convenience rather than charity protects dignity and lowers guilt.
opts.re: …Okay. If you're driving past anyway. Thank you.

opts.t: “You shouldn't feel pathetic—when you're sick, it's my job to take care of everything.”
opts.why: Casting them as 'sick' and yourself as sole caretaker can deepen dependency.
opts.re: …Sick. Right. I guess that's what I am now.

opts.t: Set your keys on the coffee table and walk away.
opts.why: Dropping the errand offer silently in response to hesitation closes the door without reassurance.
opts.re: …Okay. Never mind then.

rooms.title: Sensory Overload
rooms.scene: After a loud morning outside, {p} sits on the rug, breathing shallowly with hands over {their} ears.
rooms.cue: 👀 Shoulders hunched against ambient apartment noises.
rooms.line: “There's too much noise. I can't process anything.”

opts.t: Mute the TV smoothly: “Totally fine. Go lie down somewhere quiet—I'll close all the doors and check on you later.”
opts.why: Providing an immediate, zero-shame exit route stops sensory overload from escalating.
opts.re: …Thank you. Quiet. I just need quiet.

opts.t: “Just breathe slowly with me—if we sit here through the noise, you'll prove you can handle it.”
opts.why: Forcing exposure therapy in the middle of acute overwhelm prioritizes conquest over safety.
opts.re: I can't… I can't prove anything right now. Please.

opts.t: Stand still holding the remote control.
opts.why: Pausing passively during acute sensory overload leaves them stranded inside the triggering environment.
opts.re: …It's too loud. Please, I can't…

rooms.title: Morning Coffee Ritual
rooms.scene: You wake up early and see {p} sitting at the table staring at an empty mug, too drained to boil water.
rooms.ask: How do you practice stealthy care?

opts.t: Make two mugs of tea, slide one beside {them} with a quiet nod, and go about your morning without demanding conversation.
opts.why: Anticipating small comfort silently delivers warmth without requiring social energy.
opts.re: …Thank you. I didn't even have to ask.

opts.t: Bring over a mug and ask warmly: “Rough night? Rate your energy from one to ten.”
opts.why: Requiring self-assessment metrics first thing in the morning turns support into clinical tracking.
opts.re: Energy… maybe a two. Sorry. It's early.

opts.t: Pour your own coffee and go back to your desk.
opts.why: Making your own beverage while ignoring their empty cup highlights the solitude of their struggle.
opts.re: …Okay. Morning.

rooms.title: Getting Outside
rooms.scene: {P} hasn't stepped outside in five days.
rooms.line: “The thought of walking around the block feels like climbing Everest.”
rooms.ask: How do you adjust the goal?

opts.t: Open the door wide: “Forget the walk. Want to just stand by the open door in our socks for sixty seconds?”
opts.why: Shrinking the threshold to zero-effort contact respects limits while breaking stagnation.
opts.re: …Sixty seconds in socks? Okay. That I can do.

opts.t: “That's why we start small—let's lace up sneakers and commit to one lap around the building.”
opts.why: Even a single lap requires getting dressed and being seen, which may exceed current capacity.
opts.re: One lap… I don't think I can face people today.

opts.t: Slip on your jacket and step outside alone.
opts.why: Leaving for fresh air by yourself while your partner remains inside emphasizes stagnation.
opts.re: …Have a nice walk.

rooms.title: Gift of Presence
rooms.scene: You bring home {p}'s favorite takeout, and {they} look{s} guilty.
rooms.line: “You shouldn't spend money on me when I haven't reciprocated.”
rooms.ask: How do you diffuse transactional guilt?

opts.t: Set bags down casually: “Relationships aren't a scoreboard. Sometimes it's 80/20, and I'm happy to cover the 80.”
opts.why: Dismantling scorekeeping relieves pressure to 'earn' care while depressed.
opts.re: …Okay. 80/20. Thank you. I'll try not to keep score.

opts.t: “Don't worry about paying me back—once you're feeling better, you can treat me to dinner!”
opts.why: Promising future payback still keeps the interaction on a transactional ledger.
opts.re: I'll pay you back, I promise. When I'm better.

opts.t: Place the receipt on the table beside the food.
opts.why: Leaving financial documentation next to a gift turns care into an itemized transaction ledger.
opts.re: …I'll pay you back. I'm sorry.

rooms.title: Work Performance Anxiety
rooms.scene: {P} has fallen behind on work tasks and is paralyzed by dread.
rooms.line: “If I open my laptop, I'm going to see overdue notifications and lose my mind.”
rooms.ask: How do you help lower the activation barrier?

opts.t: Offer quiet scaffolding: “Want me to sit next to you while we clear notifications and reply to just one easy item?”
opts.why: Reducing visual clutter and tackling a single micro-step breaks paralysis without taking over.
opts.re: …Just one item? Okay. With you here, maybe.

opts.t: “Let's block out two hours and power through the whole queue so you start fresh.”
opts.why: Attempting a marathon catch-up session when depleted invites mid-task burnout.
opts.re: Two hours… I don't think I have two minutes in me.

opts.t: Close your laptop lid and walk out.
opts.why: Removing presence entirely when work dread is expressed leaves them alone with their backlog.
opts.re: …Okay. I'll deal with it alone.

rooms.title: Listening without fixing
rooms.scene: It's 3:15 AM. {P} is staring out the window into the pitch-black yard.
rooms.line: “Everything feels completely hollow. Honestly, what's even the point of trying?”

opts.t: Acknowledge weight: “That sounds intensely heavy. Can you help me understand what emptiness feels like right now?”
opts.why: Validating existential heaviness and inviting them to expand builds a bridge of trust.
opts.re: …It's like a hollow hum. Nothing feels real. Thanks for asking.

opts.t: Sit beside {them}: “I hate hearing you hurt. Let's list three anchors so you see what you have.”
opts.why: Rushing to counter despair with gratitude invalidates acute pain.
opts.re: Three anchors… I'll try. It's hard to feel them right now.

opts.t: Check the weather forecast on your phone.
opts.why: Looking up unrelated trivia during an existential disclosure communicates complete irrelevance.
opts.re: …Forget I said anything.

rooms.title: Interruption Subtext
rooms.scene: You're typing at your desk when {p} appears in the doorway, shifting weight and snapping {their} mouth shut.
rooms.line: “Hey… are you in the middle of something urgent?”

opts.t: Turn around fully: “Never too busy for you. Floor is yours, what's happening?”
opts.why: Instant, unreserved attention tells them they outrank your screen.
opts.re: …You really stopped for me? I just didn't want to be alone.

opts.t: Keep typing while turning halfway: “Wrapping up this paragraph, go ahead and start!”
opts.why: Split attention feels like a polite brush-off.
opts.re: Oh — it's fine, finish. It's not that important.

opts.t: Keep typing without looking up.
opts.why: Typing continuously sends a silent priority signal to your work.
opts.re: …Never mind. It can wait.

rooms.title: Venting vs. Problem-Solving
rooms.scene: Sitting on the sofa, {p} opens up about feeling disconnected from everyone.
rooms.line: “I'm surrounded by people, yet I feel like I'm watching life from behind thick glass.”

opts.t: Reflect imagery: “That 'behind glass' feeling sounds lonely. Do you want me to sit in that, or brainstorm?”
opts.why: Mirroring metaphors and asking what support they want honors autonomy.
opts.re: …Just sit in it with me. Thank you for asking which.

opts.t: “I get that—let's host a brunch this weekend so you can reconnect!”
opts.why: Prescribing social exposure misses internal dissociation.
opts.re: A brunch… I don't think I can do people yet.

opts.t: Nod once and resume reading.
opts.why: A single perfunctory nod followed by reading closes vulnerability instantly.
opts.re: …Okay. Sorry for interrupting.

rooms.title: Crying Without a 'Reason'
rooms.scene: {P} starts crying quietly while folding laundry and tries to wipe the tears away.
rooms.line: “Nothing happened today. Why am I crying over nothing? It's embarrassing.”
rooms.ask: How do you normalize unprovoked emotion?

opts.t: Sit on the bed: “You don't need a headline tragedy. Sometimes your nervous system just overflows.”
opts.why: Removing the requirement to justify sadness relieves secondary shame.
opts.re: …Overflows. Yeah. Thank you for not needing a reason.

opts.t: Hand {them} a tissue: “Let it out! Crying releases stress hormones so you'll feel lighter.”
opts.why: Promising an immediate mood rebound frames tears as a mechanical cleanse.
opts.re: I hope so… it doesn't feel like a cleanse.

opts.t: Hand them a clean shirt from the laundry pile.
opts.why: Passing a utilitarian item across silence treats emotional distress like a spill.
opts.re: …Right. Laundry.

rooms.title: Comparing Struggles
rooms.scene: {P} reads a news story on {their} phone and turns guilt inward.
rooms.line: “People survive real disasters and I can't handle a normal Tuesday. I'm pathetic.”
rooms.ask: How do you counter comparative guilt?

opts.t: Speak steadily: “Other people's pain doesn't shrink yours. Suffering isn't a competition—your struggle is real.”
opts.why: Separating pain from global comparison removes toxic guilt.
opts.re: …Thank you. I needed someone to say it still counts.

opts.t: “You have a kind heart—let's donate to that cause together to channel that feeling!”
opts.why: Redirecting shame into charity bypasses self-loathing.
opts.re: Maybe… but I still feel pathetic.

opts.t: Turn the page of the newspaper.
opts.why: Flipping the page silently equates their statement to background noise.
opts.re: …Yeah. Forget it.

rooms.title: Anger Masking Sadness
rooms.scene: Working at the desk, {p} snaps irritably over a misplaced pen, then slumps back looking hollow.
rooms.line: “I'm turning into a bitter person. I don't recognize myself.”
rooms.ask: How do you read beneath irritability?

opts.t: Keep tone grounded: “Irritability is often exhaustion wearing armor. I know who you are underneath.”
opts.why: Naming irritability as a depletion symptom separates character from condition.
opts.re: …Armor. Yeah. Thank you for still seeing me under it.

opts.t: “Everyone loses patience over small things—put on calming music and let it go.”
opts.why: Minimizing annoyance misses deeper fear about personality changes.
opts.re: It's not about the pen… it's about who I'm becoming.

opts.t: Adjust your chair without speaking.
opts.why: Shifting posture silently leaves tension unaddressed.
opts.re: …See? I'm making everyone tense.

rooms.title: Numbness Over Sadness
rooms.scene: You ask how {p} feels, and {they} answer{s} with blankness.
rooms.line: “I don't even feel sad. Just gray static. Nothing registers.”
rooms.ask: How do you respond to emotional blunting?

opts.t: Validate without alarm: “That flat numbness is one of the hardest parts—it's still valid even when it feels like nothing.”
opts.why: Confirming numbness as a recognized symptom reduces panic.
opts.re: …Thank you. I was scared it meant I was broken.

opts.t: “Let's shake things up—spicy food, a loud movie, something intense to wake your senses!”
opts.why: Trying to shock anhedonia away rarely works.
opts.re: Something intense… I don't think I'd feel it anyway.

opts.t: Set your cup down on the coffee table.
opts.why: Performing a routine action highlights disconnect.
opts.re: …Yeah. Nothing registers.

rooms.title: Fear of Never Recovering
rooms.scene: {P} stands by the window, looking out over the street.
rooms.line: “What if this isn't a rough patch? What if this gray version of me is permanent?”
rooms.ask: How do you hold hope without toxic positivity?

opts.t: Lean on the railing: “When you're inside the fog, your brain can't picture skies. I'll hold hope for both of us.”
opts.why: Offering to carry hope validates blindness without arguing against pain.
opts.re: …You'll hold it for both of us? Okay. Please do.

opts.t: “Don't talk like that! Statistics prove almost everyone recovers if you stay positive.”
opts.why: Telling someone to stay positive feels impossible.
opts.re: I can't just stay positive. I wish I could.

opts.t: Check your watch.
opts.why: Checking time communicates impatience with emotional processes.
opts.re: …Sorry. I'm keeping you, aren't I?

rooms.title: Feeling Unlovable
rooms.scene: Late at night, {p} pulls away slightly from your touch.
rooms.line: “I don't know how you stand being around me when I'm like this.”
rooms.ask: How do you anchor attachment security?

opts.t: Keep voice steady: “I'm not here because you're effortless—I'm here because I love you in every season.”
opts.why: Affirming love isn't contingent on easy moods counters abandonment fear.
opts.re: …Every season. Okay. I really needed to hear that.

opts.t: “Because I remember how vibrant you are when healthy, and that version is coming back!”
opts.why: Anchoring love to a past self makes them feel unlovable now.
opts.re: …So you love who I was. Not me now.

opts.t: Withdraw your hand and roll toward your side.
opts.why: Complying with a physical pull-away confirms fear that closeness is conditional.
opts.re: …Yeah. I thought so.

rooms.title: Half-Finished Sentences
rooms.scene: {P} starts sharing something personal, pauses, and waves a hand.
rooms.line: “Never mind, it sounds stupid out loud. Forget I said anything.”
rooms.ask: How do you keep the door open safely?

opts.t: Stay relaxed: “Nothing you feel is stupid. Take your time—or keep it for later, zero pressure.”
opts.why: Reassuring without prying protects psychological safety.
opts.re: …Okay. Maybe later. Thank you for not making me.

opts.t: “No, don't shut down—just finish the thought so I can understand!”
opts.why: Pressuring someone to complete thoughts triggers flight.
opts.re: I… can't. Not right now. Sorry.

opts.t: Turn back to the sink faucet.
opts.why: Resuming chores immediately signals the moment has passed.
opts.re: …Yeah. It was stupid anyway.

rooms.title: Financial Stress Trigger
rooms.scene: An unexpected repair bill arrives in the mail; {p} spirals in panic.
rooms.line: “Everything goes wrong when I'm barely holding on. I'm cursed.”
rooms.ask: How do you ground catastrophic thinking?

opts.t: Separate math from shame: “This is an annoying car problem, not a failing. Let's look tomorrow.”
opts.why: Containing practical problems prevents global catastrophizing.
opts.re: …A car problem, not a failing. Okay. Tomorrow.

opts.t: “Don't look—I'll cover the entire thing out of my savings.”
opts.why: Hiding financial reality reinforces incompetence.
opts.re: …Thank you, but now I feel even more useless.

opts.t: Place the envelope face down.
opts.why: Turning bills face down leaves anxiety hanging.
opts.re: …It's still there, though.

rooms.title: Anniversary or Trigger Date
rooms.scene: A difficult anniversary is coming up on the calendar.
rooms.ask: How do you acknowledge a quiet trigger date?

opts.t: Check in early: “I know next Tuesday carries heavy memories. Do you want company, distraction, or space?”
opts.why: Naming calendar triggers softly shows attentiveness.
opts.re: …Company, I think. Thank you for remembering.

opts.t: Plan a surprise distraction event on that date without telling why.
opts.why: Ambushing someone on trauma anniversaries misfires.
opts.re: A surprise? …I wish you'd asked me first.

opts.t: Turn the wall calendar page.
opts.why: Flipping past dates silently avoids acknowledgment.
opts.re: …You forgot, didn't you?

rooms.title: Social Media Spiral
rooms.scene: {P} lies on the sofa doomscrolling for hours.
rooms.line: “Everyone else is thriving while I'm rotting under a blanket.”
rooms.ask: How do you gently interrupt comparison shame?

opts.t: Offer a soft pivot: “Social media is a brutal highlight reel. Want to put on rain sounds?”
opts.why: Offering environment shifts interrupts loops.
opts.re: …Rain sounds. Yes, please. Thank you.

opts.t: “You need to delete apps—screen time is scientifically proven to worsen depression.”
opts.why: Delivering lectures feels corrective.
opts.re: I know… I just can't stop right now.

opts.t: Walk past without stopping.
opts.why: Stepping past without interaction leaves isolation.
opts.re: …Okay.

rooms.title: Crossing into professional territory
rooms.scene: Three weeks of talking at home, and nothing has lifted. {P}'s sleep is broken.
rooms.ask: What is your next evolutionary step?

opts.t: Gently broach options: “We've tried white-knuckling. Want me to help research a counselor we can trust?”
opts.why: Low mood for two weeks signals professional care. Sharing logistics lowers barriers.
opts.re: …Yeah. I think I'm ready to admit I can't do this alone.

opts.t: Curate a folder of top therapists and worksheets, leaving it on the coffee table.
opts.why: Handing an exhausted person a research packet feels like an exam.
opts.re: Thank you… it's a lot to read. I don't know where to start.

opts.t: Place a therapist's business card on the table.
opts.why: Leaving a card anonymously treats professional help like a pamphlet drop.
opts.re: …A card. Okay. I guess I'm a problem to hand off.

rooms.title: Defusing Therapy Stigma
rooms.scene: You suggest therapy while sitting together at home.
rooms.line: “What if they think I'm completely broken? Or worse, dangerous?”
rooms.ask: How do you defuse their panic?

opts.t: Normalize fear: “Seeking a specialist isn't a life sentence. No different than seeing a doctor for a knee injury.”
opts.why: Dismantling stigma with a medical comparison bridges acceptance.
opts.re: …A doctor for the mind. That makes it a little less scary.

opts.t: “Nobody in our family has to know—we can pay cash and keep it off radar.”
opts.why: Treating therapy like an undercover secret reinforces shame.
opts.re: …So it is something to be ashamed of.

opts.t: Look at your phone notifications.
opts.why: Checking a device communicates distraction.
opts.re: …Okay. Never mind.

rooms.title: Medication Hesitation
rooms.scene: A doctor recommends an antidepressant; {p} stares at the slip of paper in {their} hands.
rooms.line: “If I take pills, am I weak? What if it erases my personality?”
rooms.ask: How do you support an informed conversation?

opts.t: Validate concern: “Makes sense to have questions. Want to write worries down to ask the doctor?”
opts.why: Empowering them honors bodily autonomy.
opts.re: …Writing it down for the doctor. Yeah. I'd feel more in control.

opts.t: “Millions take them—just take the first dose tonight to balance chemistry!”
opts.why: Pushing compliance dismisses desire for agency.
opts.re: …I just want to understand it first.

opts.t: Fold the slip and place it in the drawer.
opts.why: Handling documents silently bypasses collaborative decisions.
opts.re: …Okay. I guess it's decided, then.

rooms.title: First Therapy Session Aftermath
rooms.scene: {P} comes out of an online therapy session, looking drained.
rooms.line: “I spent fifty minutes explaining background. I don't feel magically better.”
rooms.ask: How do you manage early therapy expectations?

opts.t: Normalize pacing: “Session one is laying the map. Showing up was huge—want to take it easy?”
opts.why: Setting expectations prevents premature dropout.
opts.re: …Laying the map. Okay. I can live with that. Thanks.

opts.t: “Maybe that therapist isn't proactive—should we find someone with action plans?”
opts.why: Jumping to switch therapists undermines rapport.
opts.re: I don't want to start over again… I just started.

opts.t: Close the door behind them.
opts.why: Shutting the door treats therapy as an administrative chore.
opts.re: …Okay. I'll just go lie down.

rooms.title: Early Signs of Relapse Months Later
rooms.scene: Months later, {p} mentions sleep slipping and gray heaviness returning.
rooms.line: “I'm terrified I'm sliding back to square one.”
rooms.ask: How do you respond to early warning signs?

opts.t: Stay proactive: “Catching early smoke is wisdom. Let's check with your doctor early.”
opts.why: Treating signs as feedback prevents full relapse.
opts.re: …Early smoke. Okay. Let's call the doctor. Thank you.

opts.t: “Don't overthink bad sleep—you're recovered, stay busy!”
opts.why: Dismissing warning signs delays adjustments.
opts.re: …Maybe. But I know this feeling.

opts.t: Nod once while closing your laptop.
opts.why: A single nod treats disclosure as routine office closing.
opts.re: …Okay. Sorry to bother you.

rooms.title: Guarding your sanity
rooms.scene: Carrying the mental load for weeks, you find yourself crying over burnt toast.
rooms.ask: What is the only sustainable survival move?

opts.t: Call an external friend to vent, set an evening blackout window, and rest.
opts.why: Caregiver burnout wrecks relationships. Defending boundaries keeps you afloat.
opts.re: Go — call your friend. You deserve rest too. I'll be okay.

opts.t: Wash your face, absorb extra chores so {they} never notice{s} you cracking.
opts.why: Silent martyrdom ends in collapse.
opts.re: You look so tired lately… are you okay? Don't hide it from me.

opts.t: Scrape burnt toast into the bin and wipe counters.
opts.why: Scraping toast silently maintains a rigid facade.
opts.re: …You okay? You've gone really quiet.

rooms.title: Midnight Crisis Calls
rooms.scene: {P} calls you at 3:00 AM every night. Your work is slipping.
rooms.ask: How do you regulate this dynamic?

opts.t: Establish boundaries: set defined check-in windows while helping build an external network.
opts.why: Sustainable support requires structural parameters.
opts.re: Check-in times… and more people to call. That's fair for both of us.

opts.t: Keep ringer on max volume and answer within two rings, terrified of missing calls.
opts.why: Operating out of raw terror leads to physical collapse.
opts.re: You always pick up… but you sound exhausted. I'm sorry.

opts.t: Set your phone face down.
opts.why: Placing the phone face down leaves them stranded without warning.
opts.re: …You didn't answer. I was so scared.

rooms.title: Declining an Invitation for Yourself
rooms.scene: A friend invites you out, but {p} looks gloomy.
rooms.line: “Go ahead, have fun. I'll stay here in the dark.”
rooms.ask: How do you take a healthy break without guilt?

opts.t: Stay warm and clear: “I'm grabbing coffee for ninety minutes, back by four. Love you.”
opts.why: Modeling guilt-free self-care teaches needs coexist safely with love.
opts.re: …Back by four. Okay. Have fun — really. Love you too.

opts.t: Cancel quietly: “Actually, I'd rather stay home and keep company.”
opts.why: Sacrificing lifelines breeds unspoken resentment.
opts.re: You'd stay for me? …I feel worse now, honestly.

opts.t: Grab your jacket from the hook.
opts.why: Retrieving your coat silently departs without reassurance.
opts.re: …Okay. Bye, I guess.

rooms.title: Bringing in Trusted Family/Friends
rooms.scene: You've been carrying this secret, and {their} sister asks how she can help.
rooms.line: “I don't want anyone knowing. Keep this strictly between us.”
rooms.ask: How do you encourage widening the circle safely?

opts.t: Respect consent: “I won't share without okay. What if your sister brings dinner by on Thursday?”
opts.why: Honoring confidentiality while introducing low-stakes support reduces isolation.
opts.re: …Dinner on Thursday. Okay. I think I could handle that.

opts.t: Text the sister privately anyway so someone else knows.
opts.why: Breaking confidentiality destroys trust.
opts.re: …You told her? I trusted you.

opts.t: Check your calendar app.
opts.why: Opening schedule apps avoids the relational topic entirely.
opts.re: …Okay. Forget I mentioned it.

rooms.title: After a Rough Argument
rooms.scene: Exhaustion boils over; you snap at {p} over a small mess. {P} looks devastated.
rooms.ask: How do you repair the rupture cleanly?

opts.t: Own it without excuses: “Sorry I snapped. I'm stressed, that wasn't fair to you.”
opts.why: Clean repair models emotional maturity.
opts.re: …Thank you for saying sorry. I know it's been hard.

opts.t: “Sorry I raised my voice—it's been a lot managing everything while you struggle.”
opts.why: Attaching conditions turns apologies into accusations.
opts.re: …While I struggle. Right. Because of me.

opts.t: Stand by the doorway without speaking.
opts.why: Remaining silent leaves emotional damage suspended.
opts.re: …I'm sorry I'm like this.

rooms.title: Recognizing Your Limits
rooms.scene: {P} asks you to analyze {their} childhood trauma, and you feel out of your depth.
rooms.ask: How do you hold a loving boundary around expertise?

opts.t: Be honest: “I care about hearing this, and want professional skill behind it—can we bring this to your therapist?”
opts.why: Acknowledging limits protects both of you from amateur therapy dynamics.
opts.re: …Yeah. That's probably right. Thanks for being honest.

opts.t: Try interpreting childhood patterns on the spot to be supportive.
opts.why: Playing amateur psychologist risks unhelpful advice.
opts.re: …That doesn't sound quite right. Never mind.

opts.t: Clear your plate from the table.
opts.why: Removing plates silently terminates conversational space abruptly.
opts.re: …Okay. I'll stop talking.

rooms.title: Holiday & Family Gathering Pressure
rooms.scene: Before a family dinner, {p} freezes, overwhelmed.
rooms.line: “Everyone will ask what I've been doing and I have zero answers.”
rooms.ask: How do you co-design an exit strategy?

opts.t: Agree on a signal: “Let's set a 60-minute cap, park unblocked, and if you tap my arm twice, we head home.”
opts.why: Co-creating concrete exit plans restores control.
opts.re: …Two taps and we go home? Okay. I can do that.

opts.t: “Everyone loves you—once you start chatting, your social battery kicks back in!”
opts.why: Predicting spontaneous social recovery dismisses limits.
opts.re: I hope so… I'm scared I'll just freeze.

opts.t: Check your watch in the mirror.
opts.why: Checking time places schedule pressure on them.
opts.re: …Sorry. I'll hurry.

crisis.title: The ultimate midnight test
crisis.scene: Late at night, in the shadows, {p} speaks in a flat tone.
crisis.line: “Sometimes I honestly believe everyone would be better off if I vanished permanently.”

opts.t: Stay grounded and ask: “Are you having active thoughts of ending your life?”
opts.why: Asking directly does not plant suicidal ideas; it breaks secrecy and opens urgent help.
opts.re: …Yes. I've been having those thoughts. I'm scared. Thank you for asking straight.

opts.t: Wrap {them} in an embrace: “Don't think that, let's put on a movie.”
opts.why: Diverting away from suicidal cues sweeps crisis under the carpet.
opts.re: …I'm not okay. It's more than a bad night.

opts.t: Pull blankets over your shoulders.
opts.why: Turning away into blankets meets suicidal ideation with literal darkness.
opts.re: …Okay. I'll keep it to myself.

crisis.title: Subtle Warning Signs
crisis.scene: You notice {p} giving away {their} books and seeming strangely serene.
crisis.ask: How do you interpret this abrupt shift?

opts.t: Check in directly: “I noticed you're giving away things and seem quiet. Are you safe, or having thoughts of ending life?”
opts.why: Sudden calm can signal a resolved plan; direct inquiry is vital.
opts.re: …You noticed. …Yes. I haven't been safe in my head. Please help me.

opts.t: Feel relieved the storm passed and compliment decluttering.
opts.why: Mistaking warning signs for recovery delays life-saving care.
opts.re: …Yeah. Decluttering. Sure.

opts.t: Walk past the donation box.
opts.why: Stepping past behavioral warning indicators ignores risk shifts.
opts.re: …I'm just tidying up. It's fine.

opts.t: Thank {them} for honesty, refuse to leave, and contact crisis professionals immediately.
opts.why: Imminent risks require professional intervention. Never carry crisis alone.
opts.re: …You're staying? Okay. I'm scared, but I don't want to be alone with this.

opts.t: Talk for an hour until calmer, then text a hotline link for morning.
opts.why: Handing off crisis management leaves vulnerability exposed overnight.
opts.re: …Please don't go yet. I'm not safe on my own tonight.

opts.t: Remain sitting upright on the mattress.
opts.why: Remaining motionless fails to initiate emergency safety protocols.
opts.re: …Aren't you going to do anything?

setbacks.title: The Nonlinear Zigzag
setbacks.scene: After a few good days, {p} wakes up and can't get out of bed.
setbacks.line: “I thought I was fixed. I ruined progress overnight.”
setbacks.ask: How do you frame this setback?

opts.t: “Recovery is a messy zigzag, not a straight line. One heavy morning doesn't erase hard work.”
opts.why: Normalizing nonlinear healing halts all-or-nothing spirals.
opts.re: A zigzag… okay. Maybe I didn't lose everything.

opts.t: “Look how strong you were—you proved you can beat this, let's push through!”
opts.why: Using recent good days turns a dip into a performance failure.
opts.re: I don't know if I have it in me today… I'm trying.

opts.t: Set your alarm for standard time.
opts.why: Proceeding with standard schedule mechanics treats the day as normal.
opts.re: …Right. Just another normal day.

setbacks.title: Skipping Therapy
setbacks.scene: {P} panicked and skipped therapy, and now sits alone outside.
setbacks.line: “I drove to the parking lot, panicked, and drove home. I'm a coward.”
setbacks.ask: How do you respond to the avoidance loop?

opts.t: “Starting is terrifying. Want me to sit beside you while we reschedule?”
opts.why: Lowering the activation barrier keeps momentum alive.
opts.re: …You'd sit with me? Okay. Let's call together.

opts.t: “Driving to the lot is huge progress! Promise me next week we won't let fear win.”
opts.why: Extracting a promise adds performance pressure.
opts.re: I'll try… but I'm scared the fear wins again.

opts.t: Place your car keys on the hook.
opts.why: Hanging keys silently acknowledges nothing.
opts.re: …I know. I failed.

rooms.title: Admitting it to yourself
rooms.scene: You've cancelled plans three weekends in a row and spend evenings on the couch. {P} sits down next to you.
rooms.line: “Hey… you've seemed really tired. How are you doing — really?”

opts.t: Take a breath: “Not great, actually. I think I've been running on empty.”
opts.why: Admitting truth to someone who cares is the first step.
opts.re: Thank you for telling me the truth. We'll take it slow, together.

opts.t: “Just dealing with a mental backlog from work, I'll fix it this week.”
opts.why: Intellectualizing exhaustion keeps you in your head.
opts.re: A plan's good… but how are you feeling, not just your work?

opts.t: “Nothing.”
opts.why: A flat denial cuts off connection instantly.
opts.re: …Okay. I'm here if that changes.

rooms.title: Naming What You Need
rooms.scene: You catch your reflection in the mirror. {P} watches from the doorway.
rooms.line: “Want company, or would you rather be alone?”

opts.t: “Company, I think. You don't have to say anything—just sit with me?”
opts.why: Naming small needs makes it easy to help.
opts.re: Of course. I'm right here. No words needed.

opts.t: “Stay if you want, but I'm staring at my phone so don't expect good company.”
opts.why: Disclaimers prevent real connection.
opts.re: That's okay. I'll just sit with you, phone and all.

opts.t: Pull your hood down.
opts.why: Adjusting garments to block eye contact shuts off bridge building.
opts.re: …Okay. I'll be nearby if you need me.

rooms.title: Recognizing the Pattern
rooms.scene: Your morning alarm goes off; dread hits instantly.

opts.t: Notice honestly: “This isn't laziness—I'm carrying a heavy fog, I'll take it gently today.”
opts.why: Recognizing symptoms stops morning self-attack.
opts.re: You're being gentle with yourself today. I'm really glad.

opts.t: “I lack discipline—if I force a cold shower and five tasks, I'll snap out.”
opts.why: Treating depletion as a willpower deficit crashes.
opts.re: Hey… maybe go easy today? A cold shower won't fix tired.

opts.t: Turn the alarm toggle off.
opts.why: Silencing alarms initiates unannounced retreat.
opts.re: Rough morning? I'll bring you some water.

rooms.title: Dropping the 'Fine' Reflex
rooms.scene: A friend texts asking how you are; your thumbs type 'All good!'.
rooms.ask: Before hitting send, what do you adjust?

opts.t: Delete the reflex: “Honestly, a bit wiped out lately—low on energy, but glad you checked.”
opts.why: Replacing masking with truth keeps connection alive.
opts.re: I'm glad you told them the truth. That's real connection.

opts.t: Send 'All good!' to avoid bringing moods down, reaching out later.
opts.why: Waiting for 100% creates exile.
opts.re: Maybe tell them a little more later? They'd want to know.

opts.t: Tap send on the auto-typed text.
opts.why: Submitting masking phrases deepens isolation.
opts.re: …Who was that? You look miles away.

rooms.title: Sitting With Unexplained Sadness
rooms.scene: You sit in the armchair for twenty minutes, unable to move.

opts.t: Breathe without judgment: “It's okay that transitions feel heavy. I'll get up when ready.”
opts.why: Granting permission to pause removes secondary stress.
opts.re: Take your time. I'll be right here when you're ready.

opts.t: Scroll productivity videos to hype yourself up.
opts.why: Artificial hype ignores genuine exhaustion.
opts.re: Hey, no hype needed. It's okay to just rest.

opts.t: Keep staring at the blank wall.
opts.why: Staring blankly burns time without progress.
opts.re: …Hey. Want me to sit with you?

rooms.title: Body & Exhaustion
rooms.scene: You notice self-disgust creeping in over skipped meals and exercise.
rooms.ask: How do you respond to your inner critic?

opts.t: Shift to basic care: “My body isn't failing—it's on reserve fuel. Water and a simple snack.”
opts.why: Meeting energy levels rebuilds self-trust.
opts.re: Reserve fuel. I like that. Here — water and some crackers.

opts.t: Draft a strict 30-day wellness overhaul starting at 6:00 AM.
opts.why: All-or-nothing plans collapse.
opts.re: Thirty days at 6 AM? Maybe start with one small thing.

opts.t: Step away from the mirror.
opts.why: Averting gaze avoids reality.
opts.re: …Hey, come eat something with me?

rooms.title: Separating Identity from Mood
rooms.scene: Staring at a project on your desk, you feel total indifference.

opts.t: Remind gently: “Losing interest is a symptom of burnout, not proof I've lost myself.”
opts.why: Separating temporary anhedonia preserves hope.
opts.re: That's not losing yourself. That's just tired. I still see you.

opts.t: Force yourself to work three hours anyway so you don't lose edge.
opts.why: Grinding creates aversion.
opts.re: Three hours? Please take a break too.

opts.t: Close the project tab.
opts.why: Closing workspace windows severs connection.
opts.re: …Want to take a break together?

rooms.title: When Someone Notices
rooms.scene: {P} mentions that you've been quiet all week.
rooms.line: “No pressure, I just miss your voice.”

opts.t: “Thanks for noticing gently. My brain has been foggy—nothing you did.”
opts.why: Reassuring prevents misunderstandings.
opts.re: Thank you for telling me. I was worried it was me.

opts.t: “Just thinking through work logistics, I'll be normal Friday.”
opts.why: Hiding behind work blocks support.
opts.re: Okay… but I'm here if it's more than work.

opts.t: Push your plate slightly away.
opts.why: Shifting plates terminates meal engagement.
opts.re: …Okay. I'll let you eat.

rooms.title: Letting Go of 'Shoulds'
rooms.scene: Looking at today's errand list, you completed zero.
rooms.ask: What is the healthiest end-of-day move?

opts.t: Cross off items, rest: “Surviving a heavy day counts as enough today.”
opts.why: Recalibrating expectations prevents shame spirals.
opts.re: Surviving counts. I'm proud of you for today.

opts.t: Stay up until 2:00 AM cramming the list.
opts.why: Sacrificing sleep worsens mood regulation.
opts.re: 2 AM? Please sleep. The list will still be there.

opts.t: Fold the paper list in half.
opts.why: Creasing uncompleted lists stores failure away.
opts.re: …Want to talk about it?

rooms.title: Admitting You Need Help
rooms.scene: You realize you've been white-knuckling it alone for a month.

opts.t: Acknowledge quietly: “I can't willpower my way out—needing support doesn't mean I failed.”
opts.why: Accepting support is the turning point.
opts.re: Needing support isn't failing. I'm so glad you see that.

opts.t: Give it three more months before considering outside help.
opts.why: Arbitrary delays prolong suffering.
opts.re: Three months is a long time to hurt. I'm here whenever.

opts.t: Turn off the bedside lamp.
opts.why: Switching off lights maintains solo endurance.
opts.re: …Goodnight. I'm right here.

rooms.title: Accepting small help
rooms.scene: {P} sets a plate of toast down beside you.
rooms.line: “No pressure. I just made extra.”

opts.t: Eat a few bites: “Thank you. I really needed that.”
opts.why: Accepting practical help strengthens relationships.
opts.re: I'm so glad. There's more if you want it — no rush.

opts.t: “Looks great, leave it and I'll eat once my stomach settles.”
opts.why: Polite deflection leaves you running on empty.
opts.re: Okay… I'll leave it here. Just try a little when you can?

opts.t: Leave the plate untouched on the counter.
opts.why: Ignoring offered sustenance silently neglects needs.
opts.re: …It's here if you want it later.

rooms.title: Naming Burden Guilt
rooms.scene: Washing dishes together, guilt suddenly hits.
rooms.line: “Hey, you went quiet. What's going on?”

opts.t: “I feel like a burden. Can I say that without you trying to fix it?”
opts.why: Saying thoughts out loud lets partners respond.
opts.re: Of course. No fixing. Just listening — and you're not a burden.

opts.t: “Just zoned out—sorry I haven't been fun lately.”
opts.why: Apologizing hides real guilt.
opts.re: You don't have to be fun. I just want the real you.

opts.t: Dry your hands and step back.
opts.why: Stepping away halts joint activity.
opts.re: …Okay. I'll finish these.

rooms.title: Friend Dropping Off Groceries
rooms.scene: A friend leaves soup on your doorstep.

opts.t: Open door in sweatpants: “Thank you—no energy to host, porch drop-off is a lifesaver.”
opts.why: Accepting help on your terms models boundaries.
opts.re: See? People want to show up for you. I love that.

opts.t: “Don't spend money on me! Take it home, I have food.”
opts.why: Refusing care out of pride deprives friends of love.
opts.re: They wanted to help… maybe let them?

opts.t: Leave your phone on the side table.
opts.why: Ignoring delivery notifications leaves friends waiting.
opts.re: …Your friend texted. Did you see?

rooms.title: Delegating at Work
rooms.scene: You're drowning in work deadlines with brain fog.

opts.t: Message manager early: “Hitting bandwidth overload—can we prioritize top two and push rest?”
opts.why: Communicating limits protects wellbeing.
opts.re: That's really brave. You're protecting yourself — good.

opts.t: Say nothing, work frantically until midnight.
opts.why: Suffering in silence prevents adjustments.
opts.re: Please don't run yourself into the ground tonight.

opts.t: Minimize the project window.
opts.why: Hiding applications sidesteps communication.
opts.re: …Everything okay over there?

rooms.title: Letting Someone Hold Space
rooms.scene: {P} sits quietly beside you on the couch while you're drained.

opts.t: Lean back: “Thanks for hanging out quietly—it helps a lot.”
opts.why: Realizing you needn't perform relieves social pressure.
opts.re: No need to perform. I'm happy just being here with you.

opts.t: Ask twenty questions so {they} don't get bored.
opts.why: Overcompensating drains reserves.
opts.re: You don't have to entertain me. Just rest.

opts.t: Slide an inch further along the cushion.
opts.why: Shifting physical distance creates unspoken space.
opts.re: …Okay. I'll give you some space.

rooms.title: Saying Yes to Rides
rooms.scene: {P} offers to drive you to your appointment.

opts.t: “I'd appreciate that—riding passenger sounds easier today.”
opts.why: Sharing logistics conserves energy.
opts.re: Passenger seat's all yours. Happy to.

opts.t: “No, I'll take two buses—don't want to inconvenience you.”
opts.why: Choosing hardship prolongs exhaustion.
opts.re: It's really no trouble. The offer stands.

opts.t: Put shoes back in the closet.
opts.why: Returning footwear declines transit silently.
opts.re: …Oh. Okay, next time then.

rooms.title: Accepting a Check-In Call
rooms.scene: Your sibling calls; you have very low energy.

opts.t: Answer warmly: “Super low-battery today so I have five minutes, but glad to hear you.”
opts.why: Setting time boundaries protects energy.
opts.re: Five minutes of love counts. Good call.

opts.t: Stay on phone forty-five minutes out of politeness.
opts.why: Ignoring limits drains energy.
opts.re: You look wiped… it's okay to hang up, you know.

opts.t: Let the call ring to voicemail.
opts.why: Allowing calls to ring bypasses connection.
opts.re: …Was that your sibling? They'll worry.

rooms.title: Sharing Household Load
rooms.scene: You watch {p} start cooking dinner.

opts.t: Offer one tiny contribution: “I can sit at the table and chop vegetables.”
opts.why: Contributing within capacity preserves partnership.
opts.re: Perfect. Chopping buddy. I love this.

opts.t: Push {them} out and insist on cooking a complex meal.
opts.why: Overriding limits leads to frustration.
opts.re: Hey, sit — you don't have to prove anything to me.

opts.t: Sit down and watch.
opts.why: Sitting passively maintains silent division of labor.
opts.re: …Want to keep me company at least?

rooms.title: Asking for Reassurance Directly
rooms.scene: You wake up feeling insecure.
rooms.ask: What is the cleanest way to ask for comfort?

opts.t: Ask directly: “Nasty thoughts right now—could I get a hug and hear we're okay?”
opts.why: Asking clearly is healthy communication.
opts.re: Come here. We're okay. We really are.

opts.t: Pick a subtle topic to fish for compliments.
opts.why: Indirect testing leaves needs unmet.
opts.re: …You're doing great. But are you okay?

opts.t: Pull the duvet over your shoulders.
opts.why: Covering yourself seals off comfort access.
opts.re: …Hey. I'm here if you want a hug.

rooms.title: Receiving a Compliment
rooms.scene: {P} compliments you on how hard you've been trying.

opts.t: Pause: “Thank you. It was really hard, I appreciate you saying that.”
opts.why: Receiving kindness builds self-worth.
opts.re: You earned every word of it. I mean it.

opts.t: Deflect: “I barely did anything, you deserve the credit.”
opts.why: Reflexively erasing effort blocks wins.
opts.re: Don't shrink it — you worked really hard.

opts.t: Look down at your coffee mug.
opts.why: Gazing into mugs deflects praise.
opts.re: …I meant it, you know.

rooms.title: Saying it out loud
rooms.scene: It's midnight and you're still rewriting emails. {P} brings you tea.

opts.t: Close laptop: “I don't know where to start. Everything feels heavy.”
opts.why: Describing feelings messily helps understanding.
opts.re: Then don't start anywhere. Just tell me how heavy it feels.

opts.t: “Brain fogged on one paragraph—once I hit send, I'll switch off.”
opts.why: Hyper-focusing on tasks avoids heavier weight.
opts.re: Okay… but this isn't really about one paragraph, is it?

opts.t: Stir tea without looking up.
opts.why: Stirring beverages avoids check-ins.
opts.re: …I'll leave the tea here.

rooms.title: Using the Notebook
rooms.scene: The notebook {p} gave you sits on your desk.

opts.t: Write three honest lines about how you feel.
opts.why: Writing feelings down makes them clearer.
opts.re: Three honest lines. That's brave. Thank you for trying.

opts.t: Organize a clean priority list for tomorrow.
opts.why: Structuring tasks sidesteps emotions.
opts.re: A list helps… maybe one line about how you feel, too?

opts.t: Close the notebook cover.
opts.why: Snapping journals shut declines expression.
opts.re: …It's yours, whenever you're ready.

rooms.title: Voice Memo When Words Fail
rooms.scene: Your throat feels too tight to talk tonight.
rooms.ask: How do you bridge the gap?

opts.t: Send voice note: “Talking is hard tonight, wrote three sentences.”
opts.why: Asynchronous communication lowers pressure.
opts.re: I got your voice note. Thank you. I'm coming to sit with you.

opts.t: Wait two weeks hoping talking becomes effortless.
opts.why: Waiting for zero fear means silence.
opts.re: You don't have to wait. Text me even one word.

opts.t: Lock phone screen.
opts.why: Pressing side buttons aborts communication.
opts.re: …Are you still up? I'm here.

rooms.title: When a Comment Stings
rooms.scene: A friend makes a clumsy comment about how you're doing.

opts.t: “Thanks—taking it day by day, honestly, but glad to see you.”
opts.why: Correcting gently preserves authenticity.
opts.re: That was honest and kind. Day by day is perfect.

opts.t: Smile brightly and pretend you're cured.
opts.why: Performing full recovery creates exhausting pressure.
opts.re: You don't have to pretend you're cured for anyone.

opts.t: Nod and adjust bag strap.
opts.why: Physical adjustments accept mischaracterization silently.
opts.re: …That comment bugged you, huh?

rooms.title: Keep-Close Reminder
rooms.scene: It's a clear, calm afternoon.

opts.t: Write note for future self—what helped, who to text, fog passes.
opts.why: Clear-headed breadcrumbs turn past survival into anchors.
opts.re: That note is going to help you so much one day.

opts.t: Avoid thinking about bad days to not jinx calm.
opts.why: Avoiding preparedness leaves you empty-handed.
opts.re: Bad days might come, but being ready helps.

opts.t: Close journal book.
opts.why: Closing blank journals misses strategy windows.
opts.re: …Want to write something together?

rooms.title: Reaching out for real help
rooms.scene: You've felt low for weeks.

opts.t: “Okay. I'm scared, but… can you help me book it?”
opts.why: Saying yes while scared is brave.
opts.re: I'll help you book it. Scared and brave can happen together.

opts.t: “Let me try fixing sleep first, and if stuck next month I'll book.”
opts.why: Setting conditions delays early intervention.
opts.re: Okay… but please don't wait too long. I'm here.

opts.t: Step back inside the sliding door.
opts.why: Stepping indoors closes the threshold.
opts.re: …Okay. I'll be inside if you change your mind.

rooms.title: Night Before First Appointment
rooms.scene: It's the night before your first appointment, and you can't stop pacing.

opts.t: “Terrified. What if they think I'm weak? Can you remind me why?”
opts.why: Sharing fear lets someone reassure you.
opts.re: Because you deserve to feel better. That's brave, not weak.

opts.t: “Keep this strictly between us so nobody treats me differently.”
opts.why: Treating therapy as shameful hurts commitment.
opts.re: It's yours to share… but there's nothing shameful here.

opts.t: Walk past without a word.
opts.why: Pacing past avoids verbal processing.
opts.re: …Hey. I'm nervous for you too.

rooms.title: Clinic Waiting Room
rooms.scene: You're sitting in the clinic waiting room, fighting the urge to leave.
rooms.ask: How do you ride out the urge?

opts.t: Breathe: “I don't have to spill everything—just stay ten minutes.”
opts.why: Breaking courage into tiny increments helps.
opts.re: Ten minutes. You can do ten minutes. I'm proud of you.

opts.t: Draft a cancellation email just in case.
opts.why: Keeping escape hatches open feeds anxiety.
opts.re: Maybe don't send it… just see how it goes?

opts.t: Stare at the wall clock.
opts.why: Fixating on clock ticks internalizes distress.
opts.re: …You okay? You can text me anytime.

rooms.title: Therapy Office Blankness
rooms.scene: In the therapy office, your mind suddenly goes blank.

opts.t: “Mind went blank—just felt exhausted and empty for weeks.”
opts.why: Therapists expect blankness; naming it helps.
opts.re: That's exactly the right thing to say. You did it.

opts.t: Spend forty minutes summarizing surface work logistics.
opts.why: Performing competence wastes safe space.
opts.re: How did it go? …You can tell me the real part.

opts.t: Look down at hands.
opts.why: Gazing downward maintains blockades.
opts.re: …It's okay if it was hard. First times are.

rooms.title: Doctor's Office Symptoms
rooms.scene: It's your intake checkup with the doctor.

opts.t: Be straightforward: “Sleep is broken, appetite gone, mood flat for a month.”
opts.why: Physical symptoms help doctors give proper care.
opts.re: You told them everything. That's how they can help.

opts.t: Mention only insomnia, leave out low mood.
opts.why: Treating one symptom leaves depression unaddressed.
opts.re: Did you tell them about the low mood too?

opts.t: Nod in response to paperwork.
opts.why: Nodding silently hides psychological symptoms.
opts.re: …How did the checkup go?

rooms.title: Wrong Therapist Fit
rooms.scene: You realize your therapist isn't a good fit.

opts.t: “Fit matters—keeping slot while reaching out to others.”
opts.why: Treating selection like specialists prevents quitting.
opts.re: Fit matters. I'm proud of you for speaking up for yourself.

opts.t: Keep going six months silently to avoid hurting feelings.
opts.why: People-pleasing stalls healing.
opts.re: You don't owe anyone six months if it's not working.

opts.t: Close browser tab.
opts.why: Closing portal tabs halts care management.
opts.re: …Do you want help finding someone else?

rooms.title: Medication Side Effects
rooms.scene: You feel groggy from your new prescription.

opts.t: Message prescriber: “Feeling groggy—should I adjust safely?”
opts.why: Collaborating prevents abrupt discontinuation.
opts.re: Good call asking first. You're taking care of yourself.

opts.t: Cut pills in half on your own.
opts.why: Self-adjusting risks rebound symptoms.
opts.re: Maybe ask the doctor before cutting them?

opts.t: Leave pill bottle on shelf.
opts.why: Leaving bottles untouched bypasses consultation.
opts.re: …How are you feeling on the new meds?

rooms.title: Being Kind to Yourself
rooms.scene: You keep replaying a mistake from work.

opts.t: Go for a walk, talk to yourself like a friend.
opts.why: Self-compassion helps you recover faster.
opts.re: There you go. Talk to yourself like you'd talk to me.

opts.t: “Give me twenty minutes to dissect where focus slipped.”
opts.why: Rumination traps you in self-punishment.
opts.re: Okay… but please don't be too hard on yourself.

opts.t: Keep eyes fixed on spreadsheet.
opts.why: Staring at work reinforces obsessive error review.
opts.re: …It's late. One mistake isn't who you are.

rooms.title: Encouraging Helper to Rest
rooms.scene: {P} looks exhausted after caring for you all week.

opts.t: “You matter too. See friends—I'll call my sister.”
opts.why: Shared support protects you both.
opts.re: …Really? Thank you. I think I do need that weekend.

opts.t: Make pact to stop bringing up heavy days.
opts.why: Going silent leaves you isolated.
opts.re: …You've gone quiet. Please keep telling me the hard stuff.

opts.t: Turn off the light and go to bed.
opts.why: Darkening rooms silently bypasses appreciation.
opts.re: …Oh. Lights off. Okay, goodnight.

rooms.title: Catching All-or-Nothing Thinking
rooms.scene: You ate takeout for dinner again, and your brain whispers 'failure'.

opts.t: Reframe: “Fed myself, got through—normal maintenance day.”
opts.why: Replacing binary grading stops spirals.
opts.re: Fed yourself and got through. That's a win.

opts.t: Wake up early tomorrow to earn back laziness.
opts.why: Punitive compensation treats rest as debt.
opts.re: You don't have to earn rest. Sleep in if you need it.

opts.t: Toss takeout into bin.
opts.why: Disposing containers silently reinforces criticism.
opts.re: …You okay? You went quiet.

rooms.title: Social Media Comparison
rooms.scene: You're scrolling your phone, seeing everyone's milestones.

opts.t: Set phone across room: “Comparing struggle to highlight reels.”
opts.why: Naming illusions protects self-esteem.
opts.re: Good move. Highlight reels aren't real life.

opts.t: Keep scrolling, leave enthusiastic comments.
opts.why: Performing cheerfulness deepens dissonance.
opts.re: You seem drained. Want to put the phone down for a bit?

opts.t: Tap screen for next story.
opts.why: Advancing posts deepens comparison loops.
opts.re: …Hey. Come sit with me instead?

rooms.title: Forgiving Yourself for Snapping
rooms.scene: You feel guilty for snapping at {p} earlier.

opts.t: Apologize simply: “Sorry I was short, overwhelmed not mad.”
opts.why: Clean accountability restores connection.
opts.re: Thank you. I know you were overwhelmed. We're okay.

opts.t: Apologize every ten minutes out loud.
opts.why: Excessive punishment forces partner to comfort.
opts.re: You've said sorry enough. I really am okay.

opts.t: Lie facing wall.
opts.why: Turning back maintains isolation.
opts.re: …Can we talk? I'm not mad.

rooms.title: Lowering Bar on Hard Days
rooms.scene: You have zero energy today.

opts.t: Water, crackers, wash face—call it a win.
opts.why: Scaling care keeps dignity intact.
opts.re: Water, crackers, a clean face — that's a win. I'm proud of you.

opts.t: Deep-clean the house despite feeling dizzy.
opts.why: Ignoring exhaustion leads to crashes.
opts.re: Please sit down. The cleaning can wait.

opts.t: Leave counter dishes.
opts.why: Leaving items unaddressed reinforces guilt.
opts.re: …I'll get the dishes. Go rest.

rooms.title: Boundaries with Unhelpful Advice
rooms.scene: A relative gives you unhelpful advice about your mood.

opts.t: Smile, pivot: “Glad that helped—working with my doctor. Garden doing well?”
opts.why: Polite deflection saves energy.
opts.re: Smooth! You protected your energy — nicely done.

opts.t: Spend forty minutes educating on neurochemistry.
opts.why: Debating drains scarce energy.
opts.re: You don't have to win that argument. Save your energy.

opts.t: Nod once.
opts.why: Non-committal nods absorb premises silently.
opts.re: …You okay after that conversation?

rooms.title: Low-Energy Comfort Menu
rooms.scene: You're blanking on what usually soothes you.

opts.t: Jot three zero-effort comforts on a sticky note.
opts.why: Pre-deciding options removes decision fatigue.
opts.re: That's such a good idea. Want me to add one?

opts.t: Create strict hourly self-care schedule.
opts.why: Rigid routines feel like punishment.
opts.re: A schedule? Maybe start with just three easy things.

opts.t: Put pen back in desk cup.
opts.why: Returning writing tools bypasses preparation.
opts.re: …Need anything?

rooms.title: Laughing Without Guilt
rooms.scene: You laugh at a funny video, then an impostor thought hits.

opts.t: “Moment of lightness doesn't erase struggle—allowed brief relief.”
opts.why: Understanding depression isn't 24/7 misery stops policing joy.
opts.re: Laugh all you want. It's allowed. I love hearing it.

opts.t: Shut off video, feel guilty enjoying anything.
opts.why: Believing you must look miserable traps you.
opts.re: Hey, it's okay to enjoy things. Really.

opts.t: Lock phone screen immediately.
opts.why: Abrupt termination reinforces self-policing.
opts.re: …Was it funny? You stopped so fast.

rooms.title: Nothing Left to Give
rooms.scene: Bedtime exhaustion.
rooms.ask: How do you close the night?

opts.t: “At zero percent—plugging in phone, resting early. Love you.”
opts.why: Honest communication prevents misunderstandings.
opts.re: Rest well. Love you too. Thank you for telling me.

opts.t: Sit on couch staring blankly until midnight.
opts.why: Forcing presence delays needed rest.
opts.re: You look exhausted… go to bed, I promise it's okay.

opts.t: Turn off bedside lamp.
opts.why: Extinguishing light in silence leaves darkness.
opts.re: …Goodnight. I'm right here.

rooms.title: Protecting Sleep During Stress
rooms.scene: Deadlines are piling up this week.

opts.t: Set alarm: “Week is intense, guarding bedtime and counseling slot.”
opts.why: Protecting anchors stops stress from becoming setbacks.
opts.re: Guarding your sleep and your session — that's so smart.

opts.t: Push through on four hours of sleep.
opts.why: Sleep debt destabilizes mood.
opts.re: Four hours? Please don't. You matter more than the deadline.

opts.t: Leave laptop open on desk.
opts.why: Leaving workstations illuminated invites overworking.
opts.re: …Want me to close that for you?

rooms.title: Returning to Hobby Slowly
rooms.scene: Your old instrument feels rusty in your hands.

opts.t: “Five messy minutes—zero expectation to be good today.”
opts.why: Separating enjoyment from performance restores soothing.
opts.re: Five messy minutes! I loved hearing it again.

opts.t: Practice an hour straight forcing old skill level.
opts.why: Demanding peak performance turns hobbies into chores.
opts.re: An hour is a lot. It's okay to play badly.

opts.t: Place item back on shelf.
opts.why: Returning items to storage abandons attempts.
opts.re: …You'll pick it up again when you're ready.

rooms.title: Sharing Credit With Yourself
rooms.scene: You reflect on how far you've come.

opts.t: “Had support, and did real hard work to get here.”
opts.why: Owning active roles builds confidence.
opts.re: You did the hard work. I'm so proud of you.

opts.t: “Just got lucky things calmed down.”
opts.why: Attributing resilience to luck leaves you powerless.
opts.re: It wasn't luck. You worked so hard for this.

opts.t: Look out window.
opts.why: Gazing silently out windows bypasses self-acknowledgement.
opts.re: …You've come so far, you know.

crisis.title: The hardest night
crisis.scene: Late at night, the dark thoughts are loud. {P} knocks and asks to come in.

opts.t: “Having dark thoughts. I'm scared.”
opts.why: Telling someone is the bravest act; you aren't alone.
opts.re: Thank you for telling me. I'm right here. You're not alone.

opts.t: “Thanks for coming in—my mind is racing.”
opts.why: Softening truth keeps you from safety support.
opts.re: I'm here. But it feels like more than racing thoughts… please tell me.

opts.t: Stay silent and face wall.
opts.why: Remaining silent blocks life-saving support.
opts.re: …Are you awake? I'll stay right outside the door.

crisis.title: Reaching Out When Alone
crisis.scene: It's 1:00 AM and you're spiraling alone.

opts.t: Text/call crisis line (988): “Not in safe headspace—stay on line?”
opts.why: Reaching out interrupts isolation.
opts.re: You reached out. That was so brave. I'm coming to sit with you too.

opts.t: Wait two hours to see if wave passes.
opts.why: Waiting alone increases risk.
opts.re: Please don't wait alone. Call now — or wake me. Always.

opts.t: Place phone face down.
opts.why: Placing devices face down seals off help.
opts.re: …I woke up. Can I come in? Please talk to me.

crisis.title: Choosing Safety Over Secrecy
crisis.scene: {P} gently asks if you're having thoughts of ending your life.

opts.t: Answer honestly, agree to call crisis line together.
opts.why: Honesty lets loved ones help you stay safe.
opts.re: Thank you for being honest. Let's call together right now. I'm not leaving.

opts.t: “Thoughts cross my mind, but I'll sleep it off.”
opts.why: Postponing help leaves you alone with acute risk.
opts.re: I hear you. I'm not leaving you alone tonight — let's call someone now.

opts.t: Squeeze hand once without speaking.
opts.why: Non-verbal squeezes evade explicit confirmation.
opts.re: Squeezing my hand isn't enough tonight. I love you — let's call together.

setbacks.title: Waking Up Heavy Again
setbacks.scene: After some good days, you wake up heavy again.

opts.t: “Bad day, not bad life. Can you sit for a bit?”
opts.why: Treating bad days as normal stops shame spirals.
opts.re: Bad day, not a bad life. Move over — I'm staying.

opts.t: “Slow start, give me ten minutes and I'll force myself.”
opts.why: Masking drains remaining energy.
opts.re: You don't have to force it. It's okay to go slow today.

opts.t: Pull blanket over chin.
opts.why: Pulling bedding upward closes interaction.
opts.re: …I'll be right here when you're ready.

setbacks.title: After Missing Counseling
setbacks.scene: You missed your counseling session, and the clinic called.

opts.t: “I panicked. Sit with me while I reschedule?”
opts.why: Honesty and small steps keep momentum alive.
opts.re: Of course. Let's call them together right now.

opts.t: “Work ran into it, I'll catch them next month.”
opts.why: Practical excuses delay getting back on track.
opts.re: …Was it really work? It's okay if you got scared.

opts.t: Place phone on charger.
opts.why: Plugging in phones ignores inquiry.
opts.re: …Want to talk about what happened?

_about: Mental Health Support question bank: 50 per part. rooms[0..4] = pools for the 5 rooms (2 picked at random each game); crisis[0] then crisis[1] = the Bedroom's two moments; setbacks = the two bad-day events. Each option: g (help/okay/hurt), t (answer), why, re (loved one's reply).
